- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the middle to late part of the horizon, particularly when true prices show upward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price spikes — forecasts lag behind actual price increases by 5–10 days.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes, then corrects downward — suggest dampening response to volatility.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to prior averages too quickly, underestimating sustained upward trends.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days.
- Model fails to capture seasonal or event-driven price surges — especially in late Q4 or early Q1, where true prices rise faster than forecasted.
